title: Recursive Hagalaz lift activates full SO(4) channel space
summary: RUN 092 implements a constant-radius recursive lift in R4 using an S2 normal-space offset and rotation-minimizing frame transport. First order occupies only the pole-bending SO(4) channels xw/yw/zw; the next superhelical order activates xy/xz/yz as well without arbitrary twist. The run also corrects the earlier reading of the eighth Hagalaz channel: tangent lock belongs to local path advance, while finite center displacement is derived by integration.
public_copy: The current Hagalaz work has moved from notation into an executable recursive geometry. A curve in four dimensions has a three-dimensional normal space, so a constant-radius lift naturally moves on a two-sphere of offset directions rather than merely tracing the circle used by an ordinary 3D helix. In the first lift only the three rotations that bend the local pole are needed. One recursive order later, all six 4D coordinate-plane rotation channels are active even though the frame transport was chosen to minimize gratuitous twist. This is a sandbox result, but it gives Hagalaz a sharper role: an eight-channel local transform whose finite sphere-to-sphere relation is obtained by integration rather than stored as eight arbitrary endpoint numbers.
